overview: A one-page Department of State list of papers concerning tin and Japan, indexing three documents filed or cross-referenced elsewhere. The entries concern conflicting Bolivian reports about Japanese tin-smelting capacity, suspected diversion to Japan of tin cargoes carried toward New York on Japanese vessels, and an intelligence report relating tin requirements to Japanese aircraft production.

people.name: Jenkins
people.role: Diplomatic official associated with despatch no. 181 from Bolivia; precise position not stated

people.name: Litton
people.role: Diplomatic official associated with a telegram from Singapore; precise position not stated

subfiles.title: Department of State List of Papers: Tin—Japan
subfiles.about: A filing list identifies three papers concerning Japanese tin smelting, shipping, and aircraft-production requirements.
subfiles.summary: The sheet records an April 3, 1940 communication from Jenkins in Bolivia requesting information about tin smelters in Japan because Bolivian reports were conflicting. It also lists a December 5 telegram from Litton in Singapore concerning suspected diversion to Japan of tin shipped on Japanese vessels for New York and requesting monthly arrival figures. A March 26 letter from the Coordinator of Information transmitted a report apparently examining tin requirements in relation to Japanese airplane production; all three entries point to other decimal-file locations.

interest: This sheet is useful as a map to related State Department records dispersed across several decimal-file classifications. Its three entries connect diplomatic reporting, commercial shipping intelligence, and analysis of Japan’s strategic-material requirements, illustrating how officials tracked tin from overseas supply and transport through smelting and eventual use in aircraft production. The references may help historians reconstruct documents no longer present in this particular bundle.
